LESSON: EATING HABITS

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES
Strand: Foods
Topic 3.2: Eating habits

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Eating habits. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which foods do I like (3 lessons) learner should be able to: consume on daily basis. and dislike?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Eating habits means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Eating habits from Kenya
3. practise Eating habits in clear steps
4. apply Eating habits in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: EATING HABITS
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Eating habits helps you succeed in HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: EATING HABITS
Study Eating habits like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Eating habits means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Eating habits means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Eating habits means in simple pupil language.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Eating habits” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Eating habits means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Eating habits from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Eating habits from Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Eating habits from Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Eating habits matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Eating habits from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Eating habits in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Eating habits in clear steps. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Eating habits in clear steps.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Eating habits this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Eating habits in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Eating habits in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Eating habits in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Eating habits in one real-life situation this week.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Eating habits” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Eating habits in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Eating habits is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Eating habits” around your school. (skill: explain what Eating habits means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Say why Eating habits matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Eating habits from Kenya)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Eating habits this week. (skill: practise Eating habits in clear steps)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Eating habits” around your school. (skill: apply Eating habits in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Eating habits to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Eating habits means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Eating habits from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Eating habits in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Eating habits from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Eating habits: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Eating habits?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which foods do I like (3 lessons) learner should be able to: consume on daily basis. and dislike?
2. Which foods are good consume on a daily basis, foods and drinks they like and dislike. for my teeth?
3. Which foods are bad  Learners are guided to mention foods that are of food and drinks they eat at for my teeth?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Eating habits means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Eating habits means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Eating habits from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
